title: two processors over one memory cell: each proves the other is alive
goal: Prove that two processors really interact through a shared memory cell. pinger watches slot 0 and counts every jump larger than its own +1 (only ponger's +10 can cause one); ponger watches slot 1 (pinger's counter) and counts every time it grows. Either program alone would see nothing, so the assertions are a two-sided liveness check rather than 'the processor ran'.
notes: Micro-processor ipt is 2/tick, so a 7-9 instruction cycle repeats roughly every 4 ticks: 240 ticks give ~50 rounds and the thresholds sit at ~1/3 of the measured value. No jumps are used on purpose -- mlog jump targets are line numbers and scene.apply_sim counts source lines, so arithmetic (op gt + op add) keeps the programs robust to edits.

assertions.desc: ponger kept adding 10 to the shared cell
pinger saw those +10 jumps (its own writes are +1, so d>1 can only be ponger)
ponger saw pinger's counter grow -- the other direction of the link
the shared value accumulated ponger's increments
text variables survive the trip too
